text:
kevin: CI flagged a regression on PR #20600 — microbench `batcher_latency` exceeded threshold, +14% vs golden. stack: perf-ci-bot posted results.
perf-ci-bot: [ALERT] pr=20600 job=batcher_latency status=FAIL delta=+14% threshold=+5% link=https://ci.internal/perf/20600
samira: ugh, I ran the same microbench locally with the PR branch and I can repro ~12-15% latency uplift on a 16k sequence workload.
jordan: any obvious culprit? kernel selection changes went in recently in 20589, and there was a batching tweak in 20595.
nina: flamegraph from the CI artifact shows a big spike in `batch_timer::wait_for_fill` and `kernel_autoselect::score_kernels` calls.
kevin: can you paste the top lines of the flame?
nina: ```
# flamegraph top
batch_timer::wait_for_fill  42.1%
kernel_autoselect::score_kernels  18.4%
kv_cache::check_and_prefetch  9.7%
nvml::sync  6.3%
``` 
samira: interesting — `kernel_autoselect::score_kernels` being that high suggests the selector is doing extra work per request instead of using cached kernel decisions.
jordan: that can blow up when batching heuristics change sequence length distribution. maybe the sampler moved prefilling earlier so hot-path misses cache.
perf-ci-bot: artifact: https://ci.internal/artifacts/pr20600/batcher_latency/flame.svg
kevin: quick bisect idea: run microbench against commit range (origin/main..pr-20600) to see which merge introduced the delta. I'll kick off a CI bisect job.
samira: I ran a local binary search and narrowed it down to commit `f3b9a2d` — the kernel selector change from PR 20589. Reverting that locally brings the microbench back within 1% of baseline.
jordan: can you confirm it's not the batching tweak interacting? try disabling the batch-timer tweak in config and rerun.
samira: disabled the `batch_timer_aggressive_fill=true` flag and latency drops ~8% (still a small gap). disabling both the flag and the selector change returns baseline.
kevin: so it's an interaction. root cause likely the selector now re-evaluates candidate kernels per-batch too often; combined with more aggressive batched fills it increases CPU contention and KV prefetch thrash.
nina: KV stats from CI show kvcache_misses spiked 3.5x during the failing run.
kevin: plan: (1) hold the release merge window and block PR 20600 from landing until we decide (release-bot: please add hold), (2) open a revert for the selector portion of 20589 as a hotfix, (3) add telemetry to avoid re-evaluating selector on identical batch shapes, (4) run full CI bisect and regression matrix.
release-bot: action=hold_added scope=release/next reason="pr-20600 perf fail" by=kevin
jordan: I'll draft the revert PR for the kernel selector change and include a test that asserts selector stable decision for repeated batch shapes.
samira: I'll add a microbench unit that simulates aggressive timer fills + selector on CPU-limited machine and push to a branch for CI validation.
kevin: owner assignment: jordan -> revert PR, samira -> stress microbench + telemetry patch, nina -> add KV miss counters to perf CI artifacts.
nina: I'll upload an initial KV snapshot to the incident doc and link once done.
samira: quick commands I used to repro locally:
```
./tools/run_microbench --bench=batcher_latency --seqlen=16384 --iters=200 --cpu-bind
git checkout pr/20600 && ./build && ./run_microbench ...
```
kevin: good. once revert PR is up we should gate it behind the perf tests and try to land a minimal fix before the bigger redesign.
jordan: noted. opening revert now, will request reviews from runtime leads and perf.
kevin: thx all. please post updates here as you progress. :thumbsup:
